_comment: Single source of truth for review routing. Consumed by .claude/hooks/review-route.mjs, which review-router.sh (advisory checklist), review-gate.sh (hard gate) and route.sh (manual/pre-PR routing) all call. Never restate these path sets, the trailer vocabulary, or the exception terms in a hook, a skill, or a doc — that drift is exactly what this file exists to prevent (CLAUDE.md guardrail #1, extract-don't-copy).

pathSets._comment: Named sets referenced by rules via pathsRef / exceptPathsRef, so 'what is a test file' is spelled out ONCE. Adding e.g. .cts test support is a one-line edit here, not four edits that can silently disagree.
pathSets._testsComment: Deliberately NOT `(^|/)tests?/` — a `tests/` directory anywhere exempted deployable code like apps/beacon/src/tests/helper.ts from the hard gate. Only the top-level suites, __tests__ dirs, and files named *.test.*/*.spec.* count as tests.
pathSets._docsComment: Prose that is NOT inert is deliberately excluded: CLAUDE.md carries the binding review-routing contract and feature-flow/SKILL.md is the producer that stamps it, so a `docs-only` verdict would let the non-shell half of this whole mechanism be deleted unreviewed. Both fall through to `source` instead.
pathSets._sourceComment: Root config files are guards in their own right — eslint.config.js enforces guardrails #1 and hooks-correctness, firestore.indexes.json backs guardrail #4's 'an index regression must not be invisible'. A 500-line change to any of them used to route nothing at all. package.json is here because .claude/settings.json's permissions.allow grants by SCRIPT NAME: an edit to `"typecheck"` silently changes what an auto-approved command runs. RESIDUAL, accepted: minChangedLines means a <15-line scripts edit still routes nothing — closing that needs a hard gate on package.json, which would tax every dependency bump.
pathSets._authSurfaceComment: firebase.json carries hosting headers and rewrites (a rewrite can point hosting at a function); the seed scripts mint PRODUCTION auth claims — 'seed scripts must mint perms not just roles' was a real bug class here; deploy.yml is the keyless-CD trust boundary (WIF/OIDC per docs/ci-cd.md). ci.yml stays advisory so ordinary CI edits keep their low friction.
pathSets._reviewHarnessComment: The whole hooks dir, not just the gate file: _hooklib.sh holds hook_is_pr_create / hook_merge_base / hook_route, so a one-line edit there disables the gate as thoroughly as editing the gate itself. .claude/agents/ is here for the same reason — docs/engineering-guardrails.md names those reviewers as the enforcing guard for mistake-classes 2 and 6, and gutting a reviewer's checklist used to score as 'docs-only, skip reviews'. An enforcement control that can be weakened unreviewed is not a control.

lighterReview._comment: A diff whose every changed file matches one of these is eligible for the lighter-review exception, as is a diff that trips no rule at all (verdict `minor`).
exceptionTerms: Full review skills MAY be skipped. They are not skipped silently:
2. record the correctness gate — full test sweep + the invariant you assert
(e.g. "zero refs remain"), with the command output.

rules.why: auth / Firestore-rules / Cloud-Functions surface — a bad write here is a production data-access hole
rules._exceptComment: Markdown under a sensitive dir cannot change deployed behavior — hard-gating apps/beacon/README.md was a false mandate. Directory-scoped CLAUDE.md files are excepted here too: they ARE instructions (so they route code-review/simplify via `source`), but blocking a PR over prose is friction without a threat. The enforcement mechanism itself — .claude/hooks, .claude/agents, the rubric, settings.json — stays hard-gated via reviewHarness.

rules.why: rules ⟷ repository access alignment, least-privilege, soft-delete invariants
Cloud Functions readiness: admin-SDK-only, input validation, idempotency, bounded queries
correctness bugs in product or harness source
rules._userInvoked: /code-review is user-invocation-only — the agent cannot launch it. The agent must either ASK the user to run it, or run an equivalent adversarial correctness pass via subagents and say in the PR which route it took. Never record this token as run when neither happened.

rules.why: reuse / dead code / altitude cleanup before the diff freezes
React perf checks: barrel imports, re-render churn, async waterfalls
latest secure version + Node 24 compat + CVE block
rules._exempt: Exempt when the edit carries NO dependency delta — only `workspace:*` entries moved, or a non-dependency field (scripts, engines) changed. State that in the PR instead of running the skill; never claim the skill ran.

rules.why: new route / large module / installed-dep change can breach the docs/performance.md budgets
rules._comment: Keyed on the LOCKFILE, not package.json: under pnpm a real dependency change always moves pnpm-lock.yaml, while a package.json `scripts`/`engines` edit cannot change a single byte of shipped bundle. Triggering a full build agent on the latter is a false mandate, and false mandates are how a routing contract loses its authority.

alsoWhen._comment: …or a large module lands anywhere in the frontend, route or not.
